title: Why he chose trombone: the circus trombonists
summary: He decided to imitate a trombonist in a circus side show, met George Williams, and discusses lower-position playing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: When you started, you started right on the trombone, was it very interesting? Yeah, on the trombone. How did you happen to like that better than others?

I don't know, I take my liking to trombone. There was a show that came into New Orleans, and they had two trombones. And I noticed a fellow that was playing trombone. He was quick and fast, and he could handle that trombone faster. Well, when I first started, I told fellows I was going to imitate that fellow. And they tried to disgust me. They said, you'll never play like that fellow. They said, you'll never play like that fellow. I said, well, I don't know, I'm going to try. And I kept trying and doing it wrong. You know, hard scales and minor scales and learning how to produce those tones, you know. I finally got it. I don't know, I just feel like since I heard that, I feel like grabbing up a trombone. What kind of a show was it? It was a circus. Oh, a circus? Yeah, it was a circus that came in. Circus come every September. See, every September. And the circus come around Christmas, December. And they come in town, and they bring those fellows. And they had one colored band, and they had two white bands. And that side show had these trombone players. And they really was good. They worked together, you know, harmonized. And I said from that, I said, well, I'll watch those fellows. And when I start to play them, I know just what to do, you know. And after I got through, I could play, and I met one of the fellows. He said, shucks. He said, I wish I could play like you. No. He wouldn't know if I had to do it. I said, I don't know why. I said, I paid attention to playing. Did you ever get their names of any of those? One fellow's named George Williams. He's one of the best supposed to be. He said that, I said that he was a better trombone player than I am, but he said I was better than him. So I, oh, he was wonderful.
There was one of George Williams that played in Handy up in Memphis.

Yeah. That's the same fellow, yeah. He's wonderful. He could do more with a trombone, I don't know, backwards, you know what you could say. I would play forwards, see. I practiced all that, but I never used it much, you know, but I knew it, you know. Practicing how you can find these trombone players now, they don't use backwards, you know, like that. All they know is what, forward, back, like that. But not playing back down, going down this way, they don't know nothing about that. Didn't that string? Lower position. Yeah, lower position. Make the scale right in the lower position. Keep down to your seventh position, but they never used it, see. I think that's why it's come so easier to me, too, to make all those different moves, you know, on trombone, because I played both positions, see. Played in lower position and forward, too, see.
